newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA SHORT OF BOWLERS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA SHORT OF BOWLERS.

text.p: Sri Lanka need a more balanced bowling side if they are to win test matches, captain Arjuna Ranatunga said on Thursday ahead of the team's departure for New Zealand.
Ranatunga said that bowling had always been the weakest link in five-day cricket for the World Cup winners.

"We have the best batting side in the world, and a very good all-round fielding side, but only one brilliant spinner and one brilliant fast bowler. This is not enough to bowl out a side twice," he said.
"Teams such as Pakistan excel due to the balance achieved from having two pairs of excellent fast bowlers and spinners."
The squad leaves on Sunday for two tests and three one-day internationals.
Ranatunga said Sri Lanka's new coach, former Australian test spinner Bruce Yardley, has been trying to improve the bowlers' technique since arriving in Colombo on January 20.
"Bruce has fine-tuned the techniques of all the bowlers, and concentrated on the fast bowlers, because we need more of them," he said.
Playing overseas on harder and flatter pitches needs more fast bowlers, said Ranatunga, explaining the inclusion of five fast bowlers in the touring side.

Apart from the main opening bowler Chaminda Vaas, the squad includes Pramodaya Wickremasinghe, Sanjeewa de Silva, Ravindra Pushpakumara, and the left-arm fast medium Nuwan Soysa, an 18-year-old untried schoolboy.
Yardley has also worked with spinners Muttiah Muralitharan and Kumar Dharmasena and made them bowl side-on from where they cannot be accused of throwing, Ranatunga said.

Off-spinner Muralitharan, who has an unorthodox action which gives him prodigious turn, was the centre of a storm during Sri Lanka's acrimonious 1995/1996 tour of Australia where he was repeatedly called for throwing.
Ranatunga, said he was confident that the Sri Lankan will do well on New Zealand's harder pitches.
He said the team had recovered well from the departure of former coach Dav Watmore and veteran number three batsman Asanka Gurusinha, who has been replaced by Marvan Atapattu.
Defending his team's performance since the World Cup, Ranatunga said: "Our performance in the first year of winning the World Cup has been better than other teams that won it".
Sri Lanka have won only one tournament -- the Singer Cup in Colombo-- during the period.
